correctness.rationale: For independent stationary Poisson telegraphs, the product coherence is \(f(t)^2\), where \(f\) solves \(f''+2\gamma f'+v^2f=0\). Closing the triple \((f^2,ff',(f')^2)\) yields the rational Laplace transform and nonnegative spectrum. With \(t=(\gamma/v)^2\) and \(z=(\omega/v)^2\), its derivative is \(-2P_t(z)/D_t(z)^2\). The exact factor \(P_t'(z)=3(z+16t+4)(z-(8-20t)/3)\) and positive \(P_t(0)\) reduce the extrema count to the sign of \(P_t((8-20t)/3)=-(32/27)(t-1)(343t^2+106t-17)\). This proves precisely two positive derivative zeros below the critical \(t_*\), a double shoulder zero at equality, and none above. The proof is global and analytic; 390 independent four-state resolvent comparisons and sample root-count checks passed.
